q: Still on this billing period, is the office's chosen multiplier of 2.0 a permissible value under SPP Doc. 204-A?
o: Yes, because 2.0 falls within the allowable range of 1.5 to 2.5
No, because it falls below the minimum allowable multiplier of 2.2
The SPP sets no multiplier limits for this compensation method
No, because it exceeds the maximum allowable multiplier of 1.8
n: Sec. 4.2 sets the multiplier range at 1.5 to 2.5; 2.0 falls squarely within that range and is therefore permissible. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2 / Formula section)
scenario: A Construction Supervision Group (CSG) is engaged for fulltime supervision services under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2). For one billing period: the Architect's rate is ₱500/hour and he logs 40 hours (AN); the Consultant's rate is ₱400/hour and he logs 30 hours (CN); the Technical Staff/Inspector's rate is ₱250/hour and 160 hours are logged (TN). The office applies a multiplier (M) of 2.0. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the period total ₱15,000.

q: Per Sec. 5.1, how is the Construction Supervision Group (CSG) described?
o: It is a government inspection bureau under the DPWH
It may be a qualified architectural firm, or one of which the Architect is only a part
It must always be a single individually licensed architect acting alone
It is always a subsidiary company of the Contractor
n: Sec. 5.1 describes the CSG as one which may be a qualified architectural firm, or one of which the Architect is only part. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 5.1)

q: Per Sec. 7.2, aside from their degree, what additional qualification must CSG Inspectors have?
o: Fluency in at least one foreign language
A separate PRC license specifically as a building inspector
Prior work experience as a local government building official
Extensive experience in design and building construction, and must be very knowledgeable in building materials and construction detailing
n: Sec. 7.2 requires extensive experience in design and building construction, with strong knowledge of building materials and construction detailing. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 7.2)

q: Where are the detailed tasks under each scope-of-services item (Sec. 2) specified?
o: In the National Building Code IRR
Under the Architect's Guidelines
In the Owner's project manual
In the Contractor's method statement
n: Sec. 2 closes by stating that the detailed tasks shall be as specified under the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 2)

q: Using the SPP Doc. 204-A formula (Direct Cost = AN + CN + TN), what is the Direct Cost for the billing period?
scenario: A Construction Supervision Group (CSG) is engaged for fulltime supervision services under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2). For one billing period: the Architect's rate is ₱500/hour and he logs 40 hours (AN); the Consultant's rate is ₱400/hour and he logs 30 hours (CN); the Technical Staff/Inspector's rate is ₱250/hour and 160 hours are logged (TN). The office applies a multiplier (M) of 2.0. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the period total ₱15,000.

q: An Owner asks an Architect to attend a project-related conference, conduct an ocular inspection of a possible project site, and confer with others about a prospective investment. Under SPP Doc. 204-A, what compensation method covers these activities?
o: Lump Sum or Fixed Fee (Sec. 4.4)
Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses (Sec. 4.2)
Percentage of Project Construction Cost (Sec. 4.1)
Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses (Sec. 4.5)
n: Sec. 4.5 covers exactly these activities — attending project-related meetings/conferences/trips (4.5.1), conducting ocular inspection of possible project sites (4.5.2), and conferring on prospective investments or ventures (4.5.3) — compensated on a per diem and honorarium basis plus out-of-pocket expenses. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.5)

q: A CSG is engaged under a Service Contract/Agreement with the Owner that makes it party to the review, evaluation, and interpretation of the Contract Documents during construction. Per Sec. 6.2, can this CSG still incur professional responsibilities and civil liabilities despite Article 1723?
o: No — Article 1723 categorically bars any liability for a CSG under any circumstance
No — only the Owner may ever be held liable for construction-phase disputes
Yes — the Service Contract/Agreement between the CSG and Owner may stipulate certain professional responsibilities and civil liabilities, particularly given this role
Yes, but only if the CSG is also the Architect-of-record
n: Sec. 6.2 states that a Service Contract/Agreement between the CSG and the Owner may stipulate certain professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of the CSG, particularly if the CSG is party to the review of the Contract Documents and their subsequent evaluation and interpretation during construction. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 6.2)

q: Per Sec. 1.3, what was the traditional term for the individual who assisted the Architect in construction inspection before full-time construction supervision groups became necessary?
o: Resident Engineer
Site Superintendent
Clerk-of-Works
Project Coordinator
n: Sec. 1.3 recounts that when projects were still manageable in size, the Architect was assisted by a construction inspector traditionally called the Clerk-of-Works; as projects grew more complex, a full-time construction supervision group became necessary. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 1.3)

q: Per Sec. 4.2, the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses cost-based method of compensation is applicable only to what kind of work?
o: Structural engineering design exclusively
Non-creative work such as accounting, secretarial, research, data gathering and preparation of reports
Legal contract negotiation with the Contractor
Purely creative architectural design work
n: Sec. 4.2 limits this method to non-creative work (accounting, secretarial, research, data gathering, report preparation and the like), since the value of creative design cannot be measured by time spent. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2)

q: Under the definition of Reimbursable Expenses (R), the cost of printing extra sets of drawings, reports, maps and contract documents is chargeable to the Client only once it exceeds how many copies submitted to the Client?
o: Five (5) copies
Ten (10) copies
Printing costs are never reimbursable
Seven (7) copies
n: The formula section states that R includes the cost of printing extra sets of drawings, reports, maps, contract documents, etc., over the seven (7) copies submitted to the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Formula section (definition of R))

q: Per Sec. 5.2, on what kind of matters is the CSG barred from making decisions?
o: Matters that are the sole responsibility of the Owner's accountant
Matters that are the sole responsibility of the Contractor
Matters that are the sole responsibility of the local government unit
Matters that are the sole responsibility of the Architect-of-record (Aor)
n: Sec. 5.2 states the CSG shall not make decisions on matters that are the sole responsibility of the Architect-of-record (Aor). (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 5.2)

q: What service does SPP Document 204-A govern, and what earlier document does it replace?
o: Predesign Services; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 201
Post-Construction Services; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 205
Fulltime Supervision Services; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 204-A
Design-Build Services; an entirely new document with no predecessor
n: SPP Document 204-A is captioned “Standard of Professional Practice on Fulltime Supervision Services” and is expressly noted as replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 204-A. (Source: SPP Document 204-A, title block)

q: Per Sec. 3.2, what is the second manner by which fulltime supervision services may be provided?
o: Working as an unpaid volunteer inspector for the Owner
Working solely as Consulting Architect for fulltime supervision services only, or as the CSG (without also being Aor)
Working exclusively under a design-build arrangement
Working as a subcontractor directly hired by the Contractor
n: Sec. 3.2 provides the second manner: working as Consulting Architect for fulltime supervision services only, or as the CSG, distinct from the dual-capacity arrangement under Sec. 3.1. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 3.2)

q: Continuing the same billing period, what is the Total Cost of Service that should be charged to the Client?
n: Total Cost of Service = Fee + R = ₱144,000 + ₱15,000 (reimbursable expenses) = ₱159,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Formula section (Total Cost of Service = Fee + R))
scenario: A Construction Supervision Group (CSG) is engaged for fulltime supervision services under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2). For one billing period: the Architect's rate is ₱500/hour and he logs 40 hours (AN); the Consultant's rate is ₱400/hour and he logs 30 hours (CN); the Technical Staff/Inspector's rate is ₱250/hour and 160 hours are logged (TN). The office applies a multiplier (M) of 2.0. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the period total ₱15,000.

q: Per Sec. 4.6 (Mixed Methods of Compensation), how does the SPP treat the choice of compensation method for a given project?
o: Mixed compensation methods are expressly prohibited under the SPP
Only a single compensation method may ever be applied per project, with no exceptions
The SPP provides for more than one method of compensation on a project, and each project should be examined to determine the most appropriate method
Mixed methods are permitted only for government-funded projects
n: Sec. 4.6 states the SPP provides for more than one method of compensation on a project, and each project should be examined to determine the most appropriate method. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.6)

q: Per Sec. 7.1, what minimum educational qualification must Inspectors of the CSG possess?
o: A Bachelor of Science in Architecture (B.S. Arch.) degree
A Master's degree in Architecture
Any bachelor's degree, supplemented by on-the-job training
A Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering degree
n: Sec. 7.1 requires CSG Inspectors to hold a Bachelor of Science in Architecture (B.S. Arch.) degree. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 7.1)

q: Per Sec. 2, which of the following is NOT part of the CSG's Scope of Services?
o: Design development of the architectural plans
Preparation of daily inspection reports and filing of documents
Evaluation of construction work
Quality control
n: Sec. 2 lists four scope items: Quality Control, Evaluation of Construction Work, Preparation of Daily Inspection Reports, and Filing of Documents. Design development is a design-phase service, not part of fulltime supervision's scope. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 2)

q: Per Sec. 4.2, what must the Architect disclose to the Client at the start of the commission before agreeing to the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method?
o: The personal home addresses of all assigned staff
The Architect's tax identification number
The rate of professionals/personnel to be assigned to the Project and the multiplier that will be applied
Only the final lump-sum total, without a breakdown
n: Sec. 4.2 requires the Architect to make known to the Client, at the start of the commission, the rate of professionals/personnel assigned and the multiplier to be applied before agreeing on this method. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2)

q: Per Sec. 4.4, the Lump Sum or Fixed Fee method may be applied especially to which type of project?
o: Emergency disaster-response projects only
Small residential renovation projects
International projects with foreign consultants only
Government projects, since they entail more paper work and time-consuming efforts
n: Sec. 4.4 states this method may be applied to government projects since they entail more paper work and time-consuming efforts. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.4)

q: Per Sec. 6.2, under Article 1723 of the Civil Code, why may the CSG appear not to have any legal responsibility?
o: Because Article 1723 grants CSGs blanket immunity from all civil suits
Because the Architect-of-record (Aor) and Engineers-of-record (Eors) are responsible for the design, while the Contractor is responsible for the construction
Because CSGs are, by law, never bound by a written service contract
Because Article 1723 applies only to publicly funded projects
n: Sec. 6.2 explains that under Article 1723 of the Civil Code, the CSG may appear to have no legal responsibility since the Aor and Eors are responsible for the design and the Contractor for the construction. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 6.2)

q: Per Sec. 1.2, who is directly and professionally responsible and liable for the construction supervision of the project?
o: The Architect-in-charge of construction (Aicc)
The city/municipal building official
The Contractor's project superintendent
The Engineer-of-record (Eor) alone
n: Sec. 1.2 states that the Architect-in-charge of construction (Aicc) is directly and professionally responsible and liable for the construction supervision of the project. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 1.2)

q: Per Sec. 4.1, where is the Architect's Fee for Fulltime Supervision based on Percentage (%) of Project Construction Cost (PCC) detailed?
o: In Article 1723 of the Civil Code
In the Uniform Code of Ethics
In the Architect's Guidelines
In the Owner's procurement manual
n: Sec. 4.1 states that the Architect's Fee for Fulltime Supervision based on the PCC shall be detailed in the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.1)

q: A CSG technical staff member is assigned to a project site 150 km from the Architect's area of operation and incurs per diem and housing costs. Is this properly chargeable to the Client as a reimbursable expense (R) under SPP Doc. 204-A?
o: No, such costs are already fully absorbed within the Fee
Only if the project Owner is a government agency
Yes, because Sec. 4's formula treats such costs as reimbursable when the assignment is over 100 km from the Architect's area of operation
No, only foreign consultants' housing and living allowances may ever be reimbursed
n: The formula section defines R to include transportation, per diem, housing and living allowance of local consultants and technical staff assigned to places over 100 km from the Architect's area of operation. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Formula section (definition of R))

q: Per Sec. 5.1, what role is the CSG expressly prohibited from assuming?
o: The role of the Owner's authorized representative for permits
The role of Architect-of-record (Aor)
The role of local building official
The responsibility of the Contractor's project superintendent
n: Sec. 5.1 provides that the CSG shall not assume the responsibility of the Contractor's project superintendent. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 5.1)

q: SPP Document 204-A, like the rest of the 2010 SPP, is Part of the IRR of what law, and when did the SPP take effect?
o: R.A. No. 545, taking effect immediately upon signing in 1950
R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004); published 21 February 2011 in the Official Gazette, taking effect 09 March 2011
R.A. No. 9266, published and effective in 2004, the year of the law's enactment
It is an internal UAP guideline independent of any law
n: The SPP series states it is Part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and was published 21 February 2011 in the Official Gazette, taking effect 09 March 2011. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A / SPP series, footer notice)

q: Per Sec. 3.1, when the Architect works in a dual capacity as Architect-of-record (Aor) and Consulting Architect for fulltime supervision (or as the CSG), why is the Aor in a better position to perform this role?
o: Because the Aor is automatically the Owner's employee under the Labor Code
Because the Aor can better interpret his own drawings and documents and assure the Contractor's conformity with them
Because the Aor alone is authorized to set the Contractor's contract price
Because the Aor legally owns the construction site during the project
n: Sec. 3.1 explains that as Architect-of-record, the Aor is in a better position to interpret his own drawings and documents and to assure conformity by the Contractor, and may assign staff to perform the fulltime supervisory work per the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 3.1)

q: Continuing the same billing period, applying the formula Fee = Direct Cost × M, what is the Fee?
n: Fee = Direct Cost (₱72,000) × M (2.0) = ₱144,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Formula section (Fee = Direct Cost x M))
scenario: A Construction Supervision Group (CSG) is engaged for fulltime supervision services under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2). For one billing period: the Architect's rate is ₱500/hour and he logs 40 hours (AN); the Consultant's rate is ₱400/hour and he logs 30 hours (CN); the Technical Staff/Inspector's rate is ₱250/hour and 160 hours are logged (TN). The office applies a multiplier (M) of 2.0. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the period total ₱15,000.

q: Per Sec. 4.5, which of the following is NOT one of the listed activities compensable on a per diem/honorarium basis?
o: Supervising the actual pouring of structural concrete on site
Conferring with others regarding prospective investments or ventures
Conducting ocular inspection of possible project sites
Attending project-related meetings, conferences, or trips
n: Sec. 4.5.1–4.5.3 list only attending meetings/conferences/trips, ocular inspection of possible sites, and conferring on prospective investments/ventures. On-site concrete-pouring supervision is a fulltime-supervision scope task, not a Sec. 4.5 activity. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.5.1–4.5.3)

q: Per Sec. 6.3, if the Aor (and Eors) and the Contractor are sued by an Owner for civil liabilities arising from acts traceable to the CSG, what recourse do the Aor and Eors have?
o: They have no legal recourse and must absorb the liability
They may file cross claims against the CSG
They may only report the CSG to the PRC Board with no other remedy
They may only terminate the CSG's service contract
n: Sec. 6.3 provides that if the Aor (and Eors) and the Contractor are sued by an Owner for civil liabilities due to acts traceable to the CSG, the Aor and Eors may file cross claims against the CSG. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 6.3)

q: Per Sec. 1.4, how is the Construction Supervision Group (CSG) engaged, and to whom is it answerable?
o: Recommended by the Architect and hired by the Owner; answerable to both the Owner and the Architect
Hired directly by the Contractor; answerable only to the Contractor
Appointed by the local building official; answerable to government only
Selected solely by the Owner without any Architect involvement
n: Sec. 1.4 provides that the CSG is normally recommended by the Architect (based on performance) and hired by the Owner, and is answerable to both the Owner and the Architect. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 1.4)

q: Per Sec. 4.2, what is the allowable range of the multiplier (M) used to cover overhead and profit?
n: Sec. 4.2 (and the formula section) states the multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5, depending on office set-up, overhead, experience, and project complexity. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2)

q: Per Sec. 4.3, when is the Professional Fee Plus Expenses method of compensation frequently used?
o: For a single, one-time small residential renovation
Exclusively for government infrastructure projects
Where there is a continuing relationship involving a series of projects
Only for emergency post-disaster repair work
n: Sec. 4.3 states this method is frequently used where there is a continuing relationship involving a series of projects, establishing a fixed sum over and above reimbursement for the Architect's technical time and overhead. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.3)

q: Per Sec. 6.1, how is legal responsibility divided between the CSG's relationship to the Owner versus to the Architect-of-record (Aor)?
o: The CSG is responsible to the Owner for both administrative and technical matters
The CSG is responsible to the Contractor for both administrative and technical matters
The CSG is responsible to the Aor for administrative matters and to the Owner for technical matters
The CSG is responsible to the Owner only for administrative matters, and to the Aor for technical matters
n: Sec. 6.1 states the CSG is responsible to the Owner only for administrative matters; for technical matters, the CSG is responsible to the Aor. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 6.1)

q: Per Sec. 1.1, which of the following is NOT one of the four principal members involved in the design and building construction process?
o: The Contractor, who performs the construction work
The Owner, who orders implementation of the project
The Architect and his Specialist Consultants (SCs)
The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
n: Sec. 1.1 lists only four members: the Owner; the Architect and his SCs; the Contractor; and the individual or group who assist in the supervision and delivery of the work. DPWH is not among them. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 1.1)

q: Per Sec. 4, on what is the Architect's compensation for Fulltime Supervision Services generally based?
o: The Architect's/firm's talents, skill, experience, and the type and level of professional services provided
Solely the floor area of the project in square meters
A fixed government-mandated rate applicable to all architects nationwide
Solely the number of years the Architect has been licensed
n: Sec. 4 states compensation is based on the Architect's/architectural firm's talents, skill, experience, and on the type and level of professional services provided. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4)
